On March 3, 1918, Bolshevik Russia signed a peace treaty that cost it more territory than almost any European power has lost in a single stroke — roughly a third of its population and farmland, gone in one signature.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Lenin wanted out of WWI at nearly any price — his government's survival mattered more than the terms. Trotsky's delegation stalled for weeks before Germany simply resumed its advance and forced a signature.

2/ The map shows the gains: Germany took the zone reaching into the Baltics and Belarus, Austria-Hungary took a slice further south, and the Ottomans picked up Ardahan, Kars, and Batumi in the Caucasus.
3/ Ukraine wasn't annexed outright — it was recognized as "independent," which in practice meant a German-backed government extracting grain shipments back to a starving Central Europe.

4/ By most estimates Russia lost around a third of its population and a third of its farmland, plus a large share of its coal and industry. Historians differ on the exact percentages, not on the scale.

5/ None of it lasted. The armistice ending WWI on November 11, 1918 explicitly voided Brest-Litovsk. Within a year the Bolsheviks were fighting to reclaim much of what they'd just signed away.

Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
